gloss: passing by each other, missing each other, miscommunication

definitions.gloss: passing each other; just missing each other
definitions.explanation: Two people or things passing each other going in opposite directions, or just missing each other in time or place.
A gap in feelings or understanding between people; a relationship where the two sides fail to connect.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧すれ{違|ちが}いになった。
examples.english: We just missed each other at the station.

examples.english: We kept missing each other's calls and couldn't get in touch.

notes:
The noun form of the verb ⟦すれ{違|ちが}う→すれ違う：02122_surechigau⟧ (to pass by each other). Has both a physical and figurative meaning.

SENSE 1 — PHYSICAL:
Two people or things passing each other going in opposite directions.
- ⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧すれ{違|ちが}いになった: we just missed each other at the station
- ⟦{電話|でんわ}→電話：01471_denwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧すれ{違|ちが}い: missing each other's phone calls

SENSE 2 — FIGURATIVE:
Emotional disconnect or miscommunication between people. Very common in relationship contexts.
- ⟦{気持|きも}ち→気持ち：02485_kimochi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧すれ{違|ちが}い: emotional disconnect
- すれ{違|ちが}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧: ships-in-the-night lifestyle (couple rarely seeing each other)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦すれ{違|ちが}う→すれ違う：02122_surechigau⟧: to pass by each other (verb form)
- ⟦{行|い}き{違|ちが}い→行き違い：09985_ikichigai⟧: mix-up, misunderstanding (logistics/communication)
